questions.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/a65b8ea83edc85a0b0ec3f3df6ee6f5bc841e9cb5d634aab963054f836965146.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le {x}^{2}+1}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y={x}^{2}+1\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y-1},
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 5,\,\sqrt{y-1}\le x\le 2},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/d10ba1db82f9d0366edb446f8bef564030fea2068066c7f05f388f0c9daa3414.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{\sqrt{y-1}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:

${\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/def6c95bc51de3e02b913d9951cce283285cd8049375c6842719c46d33a29a15.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,⟹\,x={e}^{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=e.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,{e}^{y}\le x\le e},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e38a26dbfaa0c126ec31b44f2a7d31225666779bea7b6f8b67dc2cd04e703114.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,2y-2\le x\le 2}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=2y-2\,⟹\,y=\frac{x+2}{2},
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le \frac{x+2}{2}},

questions.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Partitioned Region
questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/ea36f1ec1ddeb03dd8d133fb8d65b5d50b3fa07ba34495978d87f95742dee042.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le x}\,\cup \,{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le 4-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=4-x\,⟹\,x=4-y.
$$

To change the order of integration we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y\le x\le 4-y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e82098a4bb63f1d709a06b6a24da078594716d6a3cc0fa2e069af9dcd9154955.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y}^{4-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}-1}^{1-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e6b8889f9e8025cfca1ee0ae61b67a2f7ec9ec4aee15fab78d2f418a655bbcb8.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,{y}^{2}-1\le x\le 1-y}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/52640b30ded8bf2cd19fe7860c7640bde3c8427ae8978f32fb8020b2f7215468.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $y=y(x),$  are 

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=\sqrt{x+1}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=1-x.$ 

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{x+1}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}-1}^{1-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x+1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}/4}^{{y}^{2}/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/7212dd3ebd7ef05423c29ca6c3bd8524f8b336563d4618a960a375121c2b2157.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}\le x\le \frac{{y}^{2}}{4}}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/3eedf80b599bfaa97ad5cb42178359e24048938637f60a93e7ebb15cd8d8d2e4.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $y=y(x),$  are 

$\,$ $y=2\sqrt{-x}\,$ and $\,y=2.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=2\sqrt{x}\,$ and $\,y=2.$ 

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,2\sqrt{-x}\le y\le 2}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,2\sqrt{x}\le y\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}/4}^{{y}^{2}/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{2\sqrt{-x}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2\sqrt{x}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{1-e}^{0}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{e-1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/3426e7bdd134bc9af5a3665f8c9c55a65514afa9dca5be112eabb37479c4c9ec.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type II regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={(x,y)\,:\,1-e\le y\le 0,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)\le x\le 1}\,\cup \,{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le e-1,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)\le x\le 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)\,⟹\,y={e}^{x}-1,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)\,⟹\,y=1-{e}^{x}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,1-{e}^{x}\le y\le {e}^{x}-1},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/7d88d351b481859ec3e77350d3679387836d2e7f67325caca50e2f61cce9dcce.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1-e}^{0}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-y)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{e-1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-{e}^{x}}^{{e}^{x}-1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{\sqrt{1-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/0e338b779e846bc3f5ac981c93f9cda65b63d654c1152aa423f855d12d7978d9.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x-1\le y\le \sqrt{1-x}}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/d2d1df8652af81fbcb789ac05a2d1bf43f9b5b12f394159d0eb17b4ecec90042.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$\,$ $x=y+1.$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$\,$ $x=1-{y}^{2}.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le x\le y+1}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le 1-{y}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{\sqrt{1-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{y+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/fb111bd5365ad339dcddbf5e3d98b5e53cfc029ed88c3785154194f1e64d3297.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary is

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/0bed4692a7a6851ef2b66cb3842ebac6b2ef7ef4ff30bed41e84b7cb71c4f5c0.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}{x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3})[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3})}{4}[{x}^{4}]_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{3})]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral by Swapping the Order of Integration
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/3d51eade27c19494ac30ffdaf5baf8d30ffc9d18dcc3e1186cbc59412fe000c7.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,0\le y\le x+2}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=x+2\,⟹\,x=y-2,
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y-2\le x\le 0},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/39072bd4c2d4bd763186f4d86921eaacb990df1e862f1c60b1f764ccff422e98.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{x+2}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-2}^{0}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}[{\int }_{y-2}^{0}\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\cdot x\,{|}_{y-2}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-y){e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2(2)-{2}^{2}/2}-{e}^{2(0)-{0}^{2}/2} \\  & ={e}^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 4-{x}^{2}}.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

y=4-{x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{4-y}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 4,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{4-y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/48c874b069b55599f76a8fe1aa50c5f4db36ff8943d264a107452668d689174b.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-{x}^{2}}4x{e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-y}}4x{e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-y}}4x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}\cdot 2{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{4-y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}2(4-y){e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}\,{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & ={e}^{8(4)-{4}^{2}}-{e}^{8(0)-{0}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{16}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{-4}^{-1}{\int }_{-x-3}^{1}6x{e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/bb17a906727b436562060f84cb1acae42944587cdec6311627e30163485a72d9.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-4\le x\le -1,\,-x-3\le y\le 1}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=-x-3\,⟹\,x=-y-3,
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=-1.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 1,\,-y-3\le x\le -1},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/f80d088bb764b5dd6aa1c6d26ebd7a5b2a3894c072d81966dec4975fc0e08e59.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-1}{\int }_{-x-3}^{1}6x{e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{-y-3}^{-1}6x{e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}[{\int }_{-y-3}^{-1}6x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,{|}_{-y-3}^{-1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}3((-1)^{2}-(-y-3)^{2}){e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}3(1-(y+3)^{2}){e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{3y-(y+3)^{3}}\,{|}_{-2}^{1} \\  & ={e}^{3(1)-(1+3)^{3}}-{e}^{3(-2)-(-2+3)^{3}} \\  & ={e}^{-61}-{e}^{-7}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{8}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/d5d777577f85cd577ce35bfd3a99c1e2218622d1856f4fe7ee4afe1cfd2c9f86.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 8,\,\sqrt[3]{y}\le x\le 2}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=\sqrt[3]{y}\,⟹\,y={x}^{3},
$$

and the bottom boundary is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. Its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le {x}^{3}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/05ec37a8f4fd33c05a2438df5c5fbc697f8b560fde0b9fe73922a0db56a09c2c.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{8}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}[{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{4}}[y]_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}\,{e}^{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}{e}^{{x}^{4}}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({e}^{16}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
$\displaystyle \int_0^1 \int_{y^3}^{1} f(x,y) \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/47b8a129674d4644593741607e0efd5dea1ffde45357f327e3af4e08d0bf423d.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D= \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq1, \quad y^3 \leq x \leq 1 \big\},
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x = y^3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y = \sqrt[3]{x},
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y = 0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D= \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt[3]{x} \big\}.
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e627a8750d3f5055b3936d47100fc51ae68926dfdc0c53d020638c9ef99f9b27.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral $\displaystyle \int_0^1\int_{2x}^{3-x} f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}y\,\textrm{d}x .$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/47f6b583b2dd059ad8df49b0ca4374a964b4a28e91eb242a0dd3c7b8476fd26e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 2x \leq y \leq 3-x \big\}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/35b4b57f26c7903189899ec284faa39bb70fb3a80397b772376358d4d86b3ec1.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$$
x=\dfrac{y}{2}.
$$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=3-y.
$$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
D_1 = \Big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \quad 0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{y}{2} \Big\}
$$

and

$$
D_2 = \Big\{ (x,y) \::\: 2 \leq y \leq 3, \quad 0 \leq x \leq 3-y \Big\}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2x}^{3-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle{\int_0^{1} \int_{\sqrt{x}}^{1 } 9\sqrt{y^3+1}\,\textrm{d}y\,\textrm{d}x}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/1045aaad8025b20309b92477b4a1cf98e138064210c6fbc960c64ec26c9951df.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad \sqrt{x} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y = \sqrt{x} 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x=y^2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq x \leq y^2 \big\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/40cbaaff270daddf4b60115cc272fbc8b165b83b8823d19de2c19802617ebdb4.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}9\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}9\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}[x\,]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}3{y}^{2}({y}^{3}+1)^{1/2}\,dy \\  & =3{[\frac{2}{3}({y}^{3}+1)^{3/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[2({y}^{3}+1)^{3/2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =2(2)^{3/2}-2 \\  & =4\sqrt{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$
